keyPoints: Remote limited to TV function only; no multi-device or internet connectivity.
Core functions: next/prev channel, volume up/down, channel 1–0 toggle, and teletext (essential for hearing-impaired users).
Simplified interface with only 2–3 essential buttons; no scroll or joystick due to poor usability among elderly users.
Added features: audio signal (beep) to locate remote and on-screen button help to reduce learning curve.
Docking station considered but not primary focus; low-cost, durable materials selected for production.
summary.summary: The team finalizes a TV-only remote remote with minimal functions: channel navigation, volume, power, and teletext. Design prioritizes simplicity, usability, and affordability, avoiding complex features or multi-device support. Key additions include an audio signal to help locate the remote and on-screen button help for elderly users. A docking station is considered but not prioritized. The remote targets users aged 40 and over, emphasizing functionality over aesthetics and cost control.
summary.title: TV Remote Design Decisions for 40+ Market
